results.claim_id: R10[14] Error body code 45 described as 'org call rate limit', 1000-vs-100 contradiction
results.verifier_http_status: 200 OK (rendered in in-app browser pane; text read from main/body innerText)
results.what_source_actually_says: The quote itself matches verbatim. But the page structure attributes code 45 to the DAILY PLAN QUOTA, not the per-minute limiter. Exact order on the page: (a) 'An error with HTTP status code 429 will be returned if the number of requests made exceeds the number of requests of a particular plan.' -> {"code": 45, "message": "The API call for this organization has exceeded the maximum call rate limit of 1000."}; (b) '...if the number of requests per minute per organization exceeds 100. Users who access the application via the web interface...' -> code 44 (account variant); (c) '...if the number of requests per minute per organization exceeds 100. API customers may encounter...' -> code 44 (organization variant).
results.notes: MOST IMPORTANT FINDING OF THIS RUN. The research labels code 45 the 'org call rate limit' and frames its '1000' as contradicting the 100/min prose. The page does not support that mapping. Code 45 = per-DAY plan quota exhausted; code 44 = per-MINUTE limiter. The real (still unresolved) inconsistency is that code 45's sample says 1000 while the documented daily quotas are 2,000 and 10,000 - i.e. the sample looks stale/inherited, and 1000 matches neither number on the page. Architectural consequence: a client that treats code 45 as a per-minute limiter will retry after ~60s against an exhausted DAILY quota and stay in a 429 loop until midnight; a client that treats code 44 as a daily quota will back off for hours when a 60s wait would do. The lane's own gaps[] entry gets the 44/45/1070 ordering RIGHT while record [14] gets it wrong - an internal inconsistency in the research itself.

contradictions.what_the_research_says: Code 45 is the 'org call rate limit' error, and its sample message's '1000' contradicts the documented 100 requests/minute. Restated in R10 gaps[] as 'Body code 45's sample message says maximum call rate limit of 1000 while the prose says 100'.
contradictions.what_the_source_actually_says: The introduction page attaches code 45 to the DAILY PLAN QUOTA ('An error with HTTP status code 429 will be returned if the number of requests made exceeds the number of requests of a particular plan.'), and attaches BOTH code 44 variants to the per-minute limiter ('...if the number of requests per minute per organization exceeds 100'). Correct map: 44 = per-minute (100), 45 = per-day plan quota, 1070 = concurrency.
contradictions.why_it_matters: Retry policy. Treating code 45 as a per-minute limiter produces a 60-second retry loop against an exhausted daily quota that cannot clear until the quota resets. The residual real inconsistency is that code 45's sample says 1000 while the documented daily quotas are 2,000 and 10,000 - the sample matches neither and looks inherited from another product.

webhook_refutation_attempt.verdict: NEGATIVE SURVIVES - no outbound webhook or event-subscription API is documented for Zoho ERP
methods_used: Re-enumerated the ERP API left-nav from the rendered DOM: exactly 84 unique /erp/api/v3/<slug>/ pages, none webhook/event/notification/subscription/callback related (the /subscription/ page is recurring billing).
Mechanical scan of the first-party openapi-all.zip (78 specs, 558 distinct paths): zero webhook-management paths; the strings 'webhook' and 'callback' do not occur in any of the 78 specs.

ERP help / KB: webhooks exist ONLY as one of five workflow ACTION types (Email Alerts, In-app Notifications, Field Updates, Webhooks, Custom Functions), configured through Settings > Automation > Workflow Actions. No API is mentioned for managing them.
ERP help Developer Data: 'Incoming Webhooks' exist but are INBOUND (third party calls into ERP, handler is a Deluge script, OAuth URL or ZAPI-key URL) - not an outbound event framework.
Web search across zoho.com: webhook APIs found for CRM, Books, Commerce, Desk, SalesIQ, Assist, People and Developer extensions; none for ERP.

what_IS_available.outbound: UI-configured workflow webhooks only. Method PUT/POST/DELETE (POST default, no GET). Body: Default Payload | x-www-form-urlencoded | Raw. Security: a write-once alphanumeric secret token, 12-50 chars - a shared secret, NOT an HMAC over the body; no replay protection documented. Default Payload schema is undocumented.
what_IS_available.triggers: Documented on the workflow-rules help page (contra the research): Event Based action types Created, Edited, Created or Edited, Deleted, Submitted, Approved, Rejected - with field qualifiers 'when any field is updated' / 'when any selected field is updated' (up to three) / 'when all selected fields are updated'; plus a Date Based workflow type firing on or relative to a date field. The MODULE list is still not enumerated.
what_IS_available.inbound: Incoming Webhooks under Developer Data: generates an OAuth URL and a ZAPI Key URL, handler authored in Deluge.

webhook_refutation_attempt.residual_risk: Zoho Books - from which the ERP API is visibly derived - DOES document a full webhook management API (POST/GET/PUT/DELETE /settings/webhooks, plus /settings/webhooks/histories and /histories/{history_id}/resend) at https://www.zoho.com/books/api/v3/webhooks/ (HTTP 200). Zoho ERP already exposes a /settings/* namespace. An UNDOCUMENTED /settings/webhooks may therefore exist in the ERP runtime. Documentation-level absence is proven; runtime absence is NOT. A single authenticated GET /settings/webhooks against a trial org would settle it and is the highest-value cheap probe outstanding.
webhook_refutation_attempt.architectural_consequence_if_negative_ho: Event-driven integration cannot be provisioned programmatically. Every tenant needs manual UI setup of workflow webhooks, the receiving contract cannot be designed from docs (Default Payload undocumented), and verification is a shared secret rather than a signature. The fallback is polling on last_modified_time - which is itself constrained by 100 req/min and a 2,000-10,000 req/day ceiling.

summary.most_important_finding: R10[14] mis-attributes rate-limit error body code 45. The ERP introduction page attaches code 45 to the per-DAY plan quota and both code 44 variants to the per-MINUTE 100-request limiter; the research inverts this and builds its headline 'internal contradiction' (1000 vs 100) on the inversion. Correct map: 44 = per-minute, 45 = per-day, 1070 = concurrency. Any retry/back-off design taken from the research as written will loop 60-second retries against an exhausted daily quota.
summary.tier_note: Every CONFIRMED verdict rests on Tier 1 first-party sources (zoho.com/erp/** documentation pages rendered in a real browser, or the first-party openapi-all.zip). No Tier 3 source was used to confirm anything. The only non-ERP sources cited (CRM multi-DC, Books webhooks) are used strictly to DOWNGRADE or to bound a negative, never to confirm an ERP claim.
